weekend_summary: The inaugural Madring weekend produced an exceptionally close qualifying fight and a strategy-shaped Grand Prix. Lando Norris took pole in 1:31.824, just 0.011s ahead of Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen third. Norris led the opening phase, but a Virtual Safety Car gave Antonelli a cheap stop while Norris also lost time in a slower pit stop. Antonelli took the net lead and won ahead of Verstappen and Norris. The weekend should therefore be read as a combination of genuine front-running pace and race-execution effects, not as a strategy-neutral finishing-order comparison.

Q.summary: Norris took pole in 1:31.824, 0.011s ahead of Antonelli, with Verstappen third.

key_moments.text: Norris claimed the first Madring pole with a 1:31.824.
Antonelli was only 0.011s slower, while Verstappen qualified third.
Hamilton and Leclerc qualified fourth and fifth, with Russell sixth and Piastri seventh.

R.summary: Antonelli won ahead of Verstappen and Norris after the VSC and pit-stop sequence changed the effective race order.

key_moments.text: Norris led the opening phase from pole.
A Virtual Safety Car gave Antonelli a strategically cheap stop and moved him into the effective lead.
Norris lost additional time with a slow pit stop and rejoined behind Antonelli and Verstappen.
Antonelli won by 4.351s over Verstappen, with Norris third at +5.089s.

ANT.name: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Antonelli paired front-row qualifying pace with a victory, but the decisive track-position swing came through VSC timing rather than an on-track pass for the lead.

details.text: His result is a combined pace-and-execution signal rather than a clean strategy-neutral pace test.

NOR.name: Lando Norris
NOR.summary: Norris took pole and led the opening phase, but the VSC timing and pit execution cost him the lead.

details.text: P3 understates the competitiveness shown by his pole and early-race track position.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.summary: Verstappen qualified third and finished second, remaining close enough to pressure Mercedes and McLaren late in the race.

details.text: Red Bull's Madrid declaration was reliability-focused rather than a new persistent performance step.

Mercedes.summary: Mercedes combined near-pole one-lap pace with strong race execution and converted the VSC opportunity into victory.

details.text: The team introduced a small persistent front-lip refinement alongside circuit-specific rear-wing changes.

McLaren.summary: McLaren had genuine pole-winning pace through Norris and introduced a small persistent rear-wing flow-conditioning refinement.

details.text: Norris's final P3 was materially influenced by the VSC and pit-stop sequence.

Red Bull.summary: Verstappen finished second, while Red Bull's declared Madrid changes were reliability-focused.

details.text: The result should not be used to infer a new persistent aero step from the Madrid declaration.

strategy_and_conditions.text: The VSC materially changed pit timing and effective track position at the front.
As a brand-new circuit, Madring offered little directly comparable historical F1 data.
Bearman started from the pit lane with a new chassis/PU, Stroll started at the back after PU changes, and Sainz carried a three-place penalty for impeding.

performance_interpretation.text: Norris and Antonelli were separated by only 0.011s in qualifying, indicating a genuinely compressed front over one lap.
The race finishing order is not a clean pace ranking because the VSC and pit-stop execution materially changed track position.

upgrades_and_technical_context.text: Front-lip flow refinement; separate rear-wing changes were circuit-specific.
upgrades_and_technical_context.reported_intent: Improve flow attachment through steering conditions.
Improve flow onto the rear-wing elements.

upgrades_and_technical_context.text: Rear-wheel bodywork and floor-bib reliability work.
upgrades_and_technical_context.reported_intent: Reliability/load restoration rather than a persistent pace step.
Improve local pressure distribution and flow management.

upgrades_and_technical_context.text: Rear-wing trailing-edge winglet and diffuser-sidewall vane refinement.
upgrades_and_technical_context.reported_intent: Increase rear aerodynamic load and stability.

prediction_review.overall_assessment: Genuine pre-race Madrid forecasts are preserved. Qualifying comparison was reasonably close at the front, while race interpretation must keep the VSC/pit sequence separate from underlying pace. Numerical review should use the committed comparison artifacts after the lapped-car/DNF classification fix.

known_exceptions.text: The Red Bull/Racing Bulls substitution remained active for Madrid: Lawson drove Red Bull, Tsunoda drove Racing Bulls, and Hadjar was unavailable.
Final-grid penalties should be annotated as context rather than retroactively rewriting the saved pace forecast.

knowledge_limits.text: Actual ERS deployment and battery state are not public; LatentLap's energy-management signals remain inferred.
Race representative laps are not directly comparable for ERS or corner-speed interpretation because fuel, tyres, traffic and track state differ.
The VSC and pit-stop timing materially affected the race order.
The presence of an upgrade does not prove it caused a pace change unless reviewed reporting supports that effect.
